rule_hypotheses.rule: The base for the payout is the PM's final move-out itemization or statement total (or the ledger's final unpaid balance), not vendor invoice totals. If no exclusions apply and the total is under the caps, Approved = that total.
Rent for days or months after the lease end date (prorated holdover) is excluded.
Utilities, including prorated utilities and final utility bills, are excluded. This is applied inconsistently: #625 paid a 551.20 final utility bill in full (2024-07).
Pet damage is excluded: carpet replacement due to pets, and the pet deodorizing/treatment share of mixed cleaning lines. Ordinary carpet cleaning and stain removal on the same line are still paid.
Damage, cleaning, carpet cleaning, painting, trash/haul-off, lawn, rekey and small repairs (bulbs, blinds, aerator, outlet covers) are covered.
Tenant settlements collected by YRIG are NOT netted against the approved benefit. Subrogation recoveries are tracked separately.
Tenant payments shown on the ledger are applied oldest-first (rent, premiums, fees). The adjuster then works from the remaining unpaid balance and strips out the excluded items left in it.
Decline (0) when the tenant says they will pay, or has paid, the PM directly.
Decline (0) duplicate claims. The original claim (same address and tenant, earlier claim date) carries the payout. Find it by matching on address.
Test claims (Status 'Test Claim', rent 1, fake address) pay nothing and should be excluded from accuracy metrics.
The rent-based cap (rent rounded up to the next $500) was never binding in this batch: every approved amount is under both that cap and Max Benefit. So this batch neither confirms nor refutes it.
Max Benefit sometimes equals the waived deposit amount in the PM's program (#625 'SDW1000' gives Max 1000) but not always (#883's addendum waives $1,200 while Max is 1500).
Pre-12/1/2023 claims were usually paid at Max Benefit, but #50 (2023-03) was declined with no stated reason, even though its documented painting charge alone (1500) equals Max Benefit.

extraction_lessons: Scanned pages can hide the decisive document. #300's 46-page close-out packet has its first 5 pages (PM letter plus the TXR-2216 Itemization of Security Deposit) as images with no text. Text extraction only finds the vendor invoices, whose totals (1550, 1630, handwritten 1225, 2830) are all wrong. Check pages that have zero text.
Vendor invoices can mix tenant and owner charges (TRPI on #300) and include handwritten totals. Only tenant charges on the PM's own itemization count.

Propertyware ledgers (#249, #835) are newest-first. Use the header 'Total Unpaid' / 'Balance as of', and sum only rows labelled 'Unpaid Charge'; 'Paid Charge' rows are history. A ledger snapshot can predate the move-out charges (#835 shows a $0 balance), in which case the Security Deposit Transmittal or statement is the only source.

AppFolio-style 'Tenant Ledger' exports (#543, #625) are oldest-first with a running balance and a 'Total' at the end. #711's ledger is newest-first; reading the running balance in the wrong direction gives garbage. Always recompute the balance.
Ledger headers can be misleading. #625 shows 'Rent: 0.00' while rent is coded 'Rent Income SDW1000', and the sheet's Monthly Rent (1356.95) adds the recurring fees to the base rent (1239).
Mixed line items like 'Carpet cleaning, pet treatment and stain removal' (#711) need a covered/excluded split that the docs don't provide, so expect residual error on pet-related claims.
Duplicate files with a '(1)' suffix (#835) and duplicate claims (#731 vs #702) share documents. Dedupe by hash, and match claims by address to find the posted original.
Several claims ship only a form letter that references an 'attached ledger' that is missing (#50, #364). Those payouts can't be reproduced from the docs.

Comments sheet 'Row N' anchors do NOT line up with the current claim rows; the sheet was re-sorted after the comments were made. Examples: Row 51 talks about a Blue Fox 2024 dispute (claim #50 is New Heights 2023), Row 365 cites rent 1245 (claim #364 rent is 1795), and Row 884 references '#686 309 Creek Ledge'. Only trust comments that name a '#tracking' number in their text.
Docx ledgers (#883) extract with duplicated merged-cell columns. The PDF move-out statement is cleaner when both exist.
Photos, inspection reports (zInspector, MOI) and PM-software screenshots carry no dollar amounts. Classify them and skip them.
